props.title: Destiny
props.initialSlug: Death gives a woman three chances to save her lover

sections.content: Destiny stands as Fritz Lang's breakthrough masterpiece of German Expressionist cinema. This haunting anthology film follows Death (played with mesmerizing presence by Bernhard Goetzke) as he offers a young woman three chances to save her lover's soul. Lang's innovative use of shadows, geometric sets, and supernatural imagery influenced horror and fantasy filmmaking for decades. The film's structure - with its three historical vignettes set in Venice, the Middle East, and China - established a template for anthology horror that later shaped films like Dead of Night (1945) and Black Sabbath (1963).

sections.content: Lang's innovative special effects in Destiny opened new possibilities for fantasy cinema. His use of double exposures, miniatures, and in-camera tricks created supernatural sequences that influenced visual effects development through Hollywood's Golden Age. These techniques can be traced through James Whale's Frankenstein (1931) and The Invisible Man (1933), showing how German Expressionism's visual language shaped Universal's horror classics.

The film's meditation on fate, death and love resonated deeply in post-WWI Germany, where millions had died in the conflict. This theme of Death as a weary, sympathetic figure rather than a malevolent force was revolutionary, influencing later personifications in films like The Seventh Seal (1957) and Meet Joe Black (1998). Lang's humanizing approach to supernatural entities created a template for nuanced fantasy storytelling. SUBHEAD: Impact on Film Noir and Horror

sections.content: While Destiny's immediate influence can be seen in German Expressionism, its visual style and themes of fate and mortality laid groundwork for film noir. Lang himself would carry these elements into his later Hollywood work like The Big Heat (1953) and While the City Sleeps (1956). The high-contrast lighting, canted angles, and fatalistic themes became noir staples, while the supernatural elements evolved into psychological horror.
